claim.locator: Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 212302 (2005), abstract (TeX markup on the APS page)
claim.quote: The DEAR (DA$\ensuremath{\Phi}$NE exotic atom research) experiment measured the energy of x rays emitted in the transitions to the ground state of kaonic hydrogen.

key_value_text.locator: Marton (2007), section 'Experiments and results' (values from the DEAR paper)
key_value_text.note: The APS abstract gives the same values in TeX markup.
key_value_text.value: Kaonic hydrogen 1s shift ε = −193 ± 37 (stat) ± 6 (syst) eV and width Γ = 249 ± 111 (stat) ± 30 (syst) eV

name: Measurement of the Kaonic Hydrogen X-Ray Spectrum
notes: The claim quote is the abstract sentence as printed on the APS page, with its TeX markup; the numerical values are quoted from the SIDDHARTA collaboration's 2007 proceedings.

summary.plain: DEAR measured the X-rays from kaonic hydrogen, a hydrogen-like atom with a kaon in place of the electron, and from them the shift and width of the atom's ground state due to the strong force. The abstract calls the values the most precise yet obtained.
summary.technical: DEAR at DAΦNE: kaonic hydrogen K-series X-ray spectrum; strong-interaction 1s shift ε = −193 ± 37 (stat) ± 6 (syst) eV (repulsive) and width Γ = 249 ± 111 (stat) ± 30 (syst) eV; the Kα, Kβ and Kγ pattern was disentangled for the first time (Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 212302).

title: Measurement of the Kaonic Hydrogen X-Ray Spectrum
why_it_matters: The abstract states these are the most precise values yet obtained; SIDDHARTA's 2011 measurement (arXiv:1105.3090) cites them as the previous world result.
